text: "Welding" Kumar was an Indian criminal from Chennai, born in Navalar Street near Korukkupettai, originally known as Jeyakumar, and believed to be around 47 to 48 years old at the time of his death. He began his career as a welder in Tondiarpet and was married to Shanthi, with a daughter named Divya and a son named Sushil Kumar. He was accused in 25 criminal cases, including four murders, and was described by the Deccan Chronicle as the henchman of some Tamil Nadu politicians. He was accused of killing Radhakrishnan in 1985 and Lambamani in 1992, and had attacked Chera inside court complexes and Veeramani from Ayodhya kuppam. He also attacked lawyer Vijayan on his way to court. Kumar received life imprisonment for attacks on Radhakrishnan and Shanmugasundaram. He continued to resort to violence even while in prison, attacking John Pandian in Cuddalore jail and V. Mullaivendhan in Salem jail. He gained notoriety in Tamil Nadu after the attack on DMK lawyer R. Shanmugasundaram on 30 May 1995, which left him severely injured. The attack, which occurred as Shanmugasundaram was preparing a case against then Chief Minister Jayalalitha in the TANSI land scam case, sparked widespread outrage in the legal community and led to statewide protests. The local court convicted him in that case and sentenced him to life imprisonment, a ruling later confirmed by the High Court. On 10 June 2009, he was killed by fellow inmates in Puzhal Prison, having been transferred from Coimbatore prison two months prior. Prison officials stated that his murder resulted from the hostility he generated by taking control of the prison racket, in which "well-to-do" remand prisoners deposited their mobile phones with convicts for a fee.
